SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.

REPORT

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
C. & S. B. REGISTRY.
Traffic Branch J.J. Stuton,
No. B
Date April 14th 1932

Subject (in full) Result of enquiries made re the visits of Robert M. Short (deceased)
to the Traffic Office & the loss of .380 Auto. Pistol from the
Statement Office.
Made by Sub-Insp'r. J. Leslie. Forwarded by

Sir,

From enquiries made among the Foreign & Chinese Staff at the
Traffic Office, it has been ascertained that Robert M. Short was not
known personally to any of them. I myself met him once only and
that when prosecuting in a case of dangerous driving against him
at the U.S. Court in February last.

Enquiries at the Licensing Dept. of the Traffic Office show
that in all he made four separate visits there. The first in about
the middle of December last when he made application for a
provisional licence and which for some reason was not granted.
His second visit was during the afternoon of December 30th when
he was given a provisional licence, and a test paper.

He made a 3rd visit during the afternoon of December 31st
after having passed the test at Gordon Road to get a full driving
licence, but being unable to pay the fee for the same was not
given it.

His fourth visit was about the middle of January when he paid
the fee and was granted a licence. He was next seen again at
the Traffic Office early in February when he called to interview
Supt. McKenna in reference to a summons which had been served on
him for dangerous driving for which as I have already mentioned
he was brought before the U.S. Court.

In connexion with his visits to the Traffic Office Licensing
Office, I would point out that the office is situated on the 2nd
floor directly above the Statement Office which is on the 1st
floor and the offices have a common set of stairs.

It has not been ascertained that any of the Chinese Staff
of the Traffic Office are in any way connected with the Chinese
Bureau of Public Safety or any of the Chinese Authorities.

I am, Sir,

Your obedient servant,

J. Leslie
Sub-Inspector.

Officer i/c Traffic Branch.

上海公共租界工部局警务处。

报告

上海公共租界工部局警务处
刑事与特别股登记处。
交通科 J.J. Stuton，
编号 B
日期 1932年4月14日

主题（全称） 关于已故罗伯特·M·肖特（Robert M. Short）造访交通科办公室及证物室丢失一支.380口径自动手枪一事的调查结果。
由副督察 J. Leslie 制作。转呈

先生，

经向交通科的外籍及华员职员查询，获悉他们中无人 personally 认识罗伯特·M·肖特。我本人仅见过他一次，即去年二月在美国法院就其危险驾驶案对其提起公诉时。

经查询交通科执照部，显示他总共去过该处四次。第一次是在去年十二月中旬左右，当时他申请临时执照，但因某种原因未获批准。第二次是在十二月三十日下午，当时向他颁发了临时执照及一份测试卷。

第三次是在十二月三十一日下午，他在戈登路（Gordon Road）通过测试后前来领取正式驾驶执照，但因无法支付相应费用而未获发给。

第四次是在一月中旬左右，当时他缴纳了费用并获发了执照。此后于二月初在交通科再次见到他，当时他前来拜访麦肯纳（McKenna）总监，事由是涉及向其送达的一张危险驾驶传票，正如前文所述，他因此被提审至美国法院。

关于他造访交通科执照部一事，需指出的是，该办公室位于二楼，正下方是一楼的证物室（Statement Office），两处办公室共用一部楼梯。

尚未查明交通科的任何华员职员与中国公安局或任何中国当局有任何关联。

此致，

您顺从的仆人，

J. Leslie
副督察。

交通科主管警官。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
C. & S. B. REGISTRY.
No. D 3530.
Date 19/4/32

April 19, 2.

Sir,

I have the honour to acknowledge receipt
of one Colt .38 automatic pistol, No.2639, the
property of the Shanghai Municipal Police, found
amongst the effects of the late Mr. R. M. Short,
and have to inform you that the weapon in question
was stolen from the Traffic Department of the
Municipal Police on December 30, 1931. Investi-
gations are now in hand regarding the theft of
this pistol.

I have the honour to be,
Sir,
Your obedient servant,

〔签名〕
D. C. (CRIME)
Commissioner of Police.

E. S. Cunningham, Esq.,
Consul-General for the United States.

编号 D 3530。
日期 1932年4月19日

4月19日，2。

先生，

谨此确认收到柯尔特（Colt）.38口径自动手枪一支，编号2639，系上海公共租界工部局警务处财产，该枪在已故 R. M. 肖特先生的遗物中被发现。特此通知，涉案武器系于1931年12月30日从工部局警务处交通科被盗。目前正就该手枪失窃案进行调查。

谨此致意，
先生，
您顺从的仆人，

〔签名〕
D. C. (刑事)
警务处处长。

E. S. Cunningham 先生，
美国总领事。

IN REPLY REFER TO
FILE NO. 330/RLS/JW

AMERICAN CONSULAR SERVICE

American Consulate General,
Shanghai, China, April 16, 1932.

DEPARTMENT OF STATE

Subject: Shanghai Municipal Police Revolver.

Major F. W. Gerrard, C.I.E.,
Commissioner of Police,
Shanghai Municipal Police,
18 Hankow Road,
Shanghai, China.

Sir:

1/      I have the honor to forward herewith one Colt
Automatic Revolver, calibre .380, marked "Shanghai
Municipal Police, No.2639", which was found among
the effects of the late Mr. Robert M. Short, an Amer-
ican citizen who came to his death near Soochow, China,
on February 22, 1932. It is requested that you kind-
ly give this Consulate General a receipt for the
revolver.

        I have the honor to be, Sir,
                Your obedient servant,

                Edwin S. Cunningham,
                American Consul General.

Accompaniment:

        1/- One revolver, as described above.
